answer: Yes. Eve is an executor, and executors may cancel runs.
explanation: R4 lets an executor run and cancel jobs, and R46 lets any member cancel a queued or running run. The access matrix shows eve's cancel as 200 (or 409 when the run already finished).

citations.quote: May view that application's job configs and runs, and run and cancel jobs.

verified.detail: Step 4 (eve cancels the queued run) answered 200 {"status": "cancelled"}, as the spec says.
verified.scenario:
1. POST /auth/login {email: root@example.com, password: ...} as no token -> 200
2. POST /applications/1/members {user: eve, role: executor} as root -> 201
3. POST /applications/1/jobs/10/runs as root -> 201 (run 200 queued)
4. POST /applications/1/runs/200/cancel as eve -> 200 {"status": "cancelled"} (claim step)
